title: Micro-review experiments and quick checks
content:
Quick context
- Purpose: lightweight checklist + ephemeral experiments to run while reviewing runtime/kv-cache/batcher PRs. Not a formal doc; notes to self and tiny commands to reproduce behaviours.
- When to use: if PR touches: batching loop, KV cache read/write, cache eviction, kernel selection heuristics, or request routing fallback.

High-level review checklist (fast pass, 3–7 min)
- Does the PR change request pathing or alter request metadata? (trace/span tags, customer_id, route)
- Any changes to key/value cache lifetime or eviction policy? If yes, verify no silent correctness regressions (cold-start tokens, stale prefill).
- Batch boundaries: are we introducing potential head-of-line blocking? Look for sleeping/wait loops or timeouts.
- Does the PR add allocations per-request (bytebuf copies, string concatenation inside hot loop)? Could it increase p99 CPU?
- Op-level fallbacks: Are alternative kernels/quantized variants still reachable? Anything that forces a slow path?
- Tests: unit + small perf harness included? If only unit tests, add TODO to run small microbench locally.

Quick repro and micro-experiments (local devbox)
- start a dev server with a tiny model (quantized toy)
  - git checkout <branch>; export DEV_MODEL=llama-mini; make dev-run 
- script to replay requests from recorded trace (use curated traces in /dev/mini-traces):
  - python tools/replay_trace.py --trace=mini_batch_kv_eviction.json --target=http://localhost:8080 
- Collect latency histogram and kv cache hit-rate:
  - curl -s http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep kv_cache_hit_ratio
  - tail -n 200 logs/dev.log | rg "kv-cache" -n --line-number

Micro experiments to validate PR assumptions
1) KV eviction edge: create a synthetic prefill scenario where many short sequences prefill the KV and then we request a long generation from same session. Expected: KV hold should persist for X ms. Test: replay 200 short-prefill requests -> single long request. Check tail-latency and memory usage.
2) Small-batch stress: run with BATCH_SIZE override to 1, 4, 8 and watch p50/p95 change. Look for non-monotonic regressions (p95 rises at 4 but falls at 8 suggests head-of-line or scheduling instability).
3) Kernel fallthrough: force a fallback kernel (set env OVERRIDE_KERNEL=slow) and confirm fallback metric increments and tracing spans annotate fallback reason.
4) Rollout fraction sim: exercise the canary routing - use `make canary-local` and toggle fraction values (0.01, 0.1, 0.5) — ensure route table doesn’t send more than allowed and that fallback to default works under capacity pressure.

Commands I keep reaching for (copyable)
- run perf trace: ./scripts/perf/run_flamegraph.sh --target=http://localhost:8080 --duration=30s
- replay a saved trace with 1000 requests: python tools/replay_trace.py --trace traces/2024-11-18/kv-thrash.json --concurrency 8
- quick mem-snapshot: curl localhost:8080/debug/mem | jq .summaries
- check canary routing: curl -s localhost:8080/debug/routing | jq .routes | rg "canary" -n

Signals to watch for (red flags)
- sudden drop in kv_cache_hit_ratio with unchanged trace (means eviction/lookup bug)
- p99 increases while p50 stable (indicates tail, queuing, or GC pause)
- increased variance between repeated runs (non-deterministic scheduling or timeouts)
- new error types in logs (panic, OOM, assertion) even if tests pass

Heuristic questions to ask in review comment
- Why this change instead of adjusting batcher tunables? (cost of code vs config)
- If this reduces mean latency, what's the p99 cost? Do we have dashboards updated?
- Does the change require a migration or config tweak for dedicated/private deployments? (runtime flags, KMS, K8s nodes)
- Are there safe defaults? Any knobs exposed to customers accidentally?

Quick unit + perf test additions I ask for
- small integration test that replays a 1s trace and asserts response correctness (not perf)
- microbench harness that runs 1000 iterations and outputs p50/p95/p99 (artifact in logs to attach to PR)
- CI flavor: run `ci/perf-lite` on PR build (fast 30s smoke) — if not added, request it.

Notes-to-self: odd cases I keep hitting
- observed a race where the KV client could race on eviction when session TTL hits concurrently with a prefill; log shows duplicated evict+read. Hypothesis: missing lock around session map when TTL triggers eviction callback.
- batching loop sometimes sleeps in 1ms increments leading to spiky latencies when load ramps (don't trust small sleeps in hot loops). Consider switch to condition-variable wakeups.
- trace traces: sometimes synthetic traces have been edited and lost headers (session_id) — ensure replay tool validates required headers before sending.

Follow-ups and TODOs
- write a tiny test harness to reproduce the KV race (owner: me) — target: reproduce within 5s on dev box. Due: next sprint.
- add `ci/perf-lite` job template snippet to repo so reviewers can re-use it (owner: Anya).
- add a note in PR checklist: "include expected impact on p50/p95/p99 or include perf artifact".
- refactor: move tiny sleep-based backoff into `batcher/waiter.go` -> replace with condvar (low risk refactor).

Quick TL;DR for comments to leave on a PR
- "Looks reasonable overall — main request: please add a microbench run artifact (p50/p95/p99) and a short note about why this path was chosen over tuning the batcher. Also add a tiny integration replay test that asserts no correctness regressions under prefill->long-gen scenario."

Scrap ideas worth saving (stash)
- benchmark a mem-capped KV (evict oldest by token weight) rather than TTL only — might smooth mem spikes under token-heavy sessions.
- small feature: diagnostic header X-KV-Reason forwarded to logs so we can tie cache misses to caller-side behavior.

End of scratchpad — will clean up into a more formal review-playbook later if these keep recurring.
